rgb: The scene is an unfinished indoor room with plastered grey walls, a high ceiling, and an elevated bamboo scaffolding platform bridging the space above a sunlit floor below. In frames 1, 2, and 5, the camera wearer looks upward toward the scaffolding roughly 0.5 to 1.5 metres away and above, where a man in a patterned shirt, blue jeans, and cap stands on the central bamboo poles facing and looking away from the camera wearer while holding a small yellow tool, and a second person in a pink shirt and jeans stands about 1.5 to 2 metres to his left (farther in the background on the left edge, roughly 3 to 5 metres from the camera wearer) facing toward the camera wearer and away from the left wall and partly cropped by the left frame boundary. On the lower-right bamboo poles about 3 to 5 metres in front of the camera wearer rests a plastering float, while in frame 2 a rectangular block is mid-air just to the left of the central man, and in frame 5 the yellow tool is mid-air well above his raised hands and out of his arm's reach. In frame 3, the camera wearer pitches their head sharply downward to look at the floor and lower scaffolding directly in front and below, where a black rectangular bucket, a mortar pan on the left, and a white circular pan sit out of arm's reach (about 3 to 5 metres away), and a blue basin lies on the floor further ahead (about 2 to 2.5 metres away) alongside the camera wearer's cast shadow. In frame 4, the camera wearer tilts their head back up toward the underside and front edge of the bamboo scaffolding roughly 3 to 5 metres ahead and above (with the blue basin still visible below on the right and the upper room obscured in dark shadow), before returning in frame 5 to the upward view of the man on the scaffolding.
depth: The depth map captures the vertical layout of an indoor construction space with multi-tier bamboo scaffolding as the camera wearer pitches their head from looking upward (frames 1–2), sharply downward to the floor (frame 3), across mid-level poles (frame 4), and back upward (frame 5). In frames 1, 2, and 5, distant values place the lower scaffolding poles and a plastering trowel far beyond the camera wearer's arm's reach at 3–5 m below and in front, while above them a partially cropped worker on the left stands at ~3–5 m (facing right/toward) and a second worker stands ~1.5–2 m closer and to the right on upper poles at ~0.5–1.5 m (facing left and looking downward in frames 1–2, then upward with a brick beyond his overhead reach in frame 5). As the camera tilts down in frame 3, the map shows a rectangular bucket and round pans on the floor ~3–5 m below (with the nearest container and poles far beyond arm's reach), before tilting up in frame 4 to show horizontal scaffolding ~3–5 m ahead. Crucially, the depth map reveals the full 3D geometry of the mid-level bamboo poles and the faint silhouette of the nearby standing worker (~0.5–1.5 m above) in the severely underexposed frame 4 that are nearly invisible in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable where it completely misses the mid-air block far beyond the nearby worker's reach in frame 2, merges narrow gaps between adjacent bamboo poles, and misinterprets flat floor shadows and dark basins in frame 3 as distinct depth surfaces.
segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only human figures against a black background, omitting the room walls, bamboo scaffolding, floor containers, and bricks across all five frames. In frames 1 and 2, it identifies the nearby worker standing above and to the right (~0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer, facing left and looking down away from the camera wearer's direction with his arms in front and a brick out of reach) and the farther worker ~1.5–2 m to his left (~3–5 m from the camera wearer, facing toward/right with his left side and upper body partially occluded by the left frame edge). As the camera wearer turns their head sharply downward in frame 3, upward through the dark mid-section in frame 4, and back to the upper scaffolding in frame 5, the two workers exit and re-enter the field of view while remaining on their respective perches. The masks make it easy to separate the background left-side worker's silhouette from the background wall in frames 1–2, but the map is highly unreliable overall. It swaps instance colours between the two workers from frame 1 to frame 2, falsely labels the camera wearer's flat ground shadow and an adjacent round pan (~1.5–2 m below) as a person in frame 3, and completely fails to detect the nearby worker reaching overhead and the left-side worker's lower leg in frames 4 and 5.
pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body skeletons on a black background without any scene geometry, objects, or farther background figures. It detects the nearby worker standing on the upper-right scaffolding (~0.5–1.5 m away and above the camera wearer, ~1.5–2 m right of the farther worker) only in frames 2 and 5, showing him facing left and looking downward away from the camera wearer/left in frame 2, and turning his head and both raised arms upward with an airborne brick out of reach in frame 5. Across the sequence, as the camera pitches down in frame 3, up through the dark scaffolding in frame 4, and back to the ceiling in frame 5, the map tracks the nearby worker's transition from a lowered-arm stance to an overhead catch posture. In frame 5, the yellow skeletal links clearly isolate the exact angles of the nearby worker's raised elbows and wrists against the dim ceiling, which are harder to parse in RGB. However, the map is unreliable because it misses the nearby worker in frames 1 and 4, completely misses the partially cropped worker on the left (~3–5 m away) in frames 1, 2, and 5, detects no magenta hand skeletons for anyone, and hallucinates a torso-and-head skeleton onto the camera wearer's 2D shadow on the floor (~1.5–2 m below) in frame 3.
